status: Bounded-exploration follow-ups; current final champion confirmations remain incomplete
scope: Explicit unresolved possibilities, not added requirements or authorization for another tuning campaign. Current task is to finish the already-declared final panels and consolidate them.

items.topic: Full delivery from fast Flint implementations
items.observed: Frame confirmation stopped at4/5 when saved regressions were omitted; worklog stopped at1/2 after timeout without final handoff despite correct implementation and evaluator greens.
items.open_question: Can a task-local completion aid or more economical verification make this speed useful without weakening the regression or finalization obligations?
items.next_test: Change one declared aid on development seeds, preserve the failed panels, then use fresh confirmation seeds if the hypothesis survives.

items.topic: Coder semantic failures versus context and call limits
items.observed: Coder initial mapping accepted3/7. Long-task revisions did not establish a general improvement; some failures were semantic and one SQLite revision exhausted the64-call limit before600seconds.
items.open_question: Which failures are improved by a more direct work plan or context recovery, and which require stronger model reasoning? Larger contexts and additional recipes remain unexhausted.
items.next_test: Choose a specific failure mechanism from the retained trace; compare one intervention under the same public contract and include correctness, final delivery and context overhead.

items.observed: Codec comparisons support task-specific selection. Official final-panel times use a ready server and explicit prefix warm-up; loading and warming are separate costs. Coder weights and startup costs are larger than the other selected models.
items.open_question: Does switching to a specialized champion pay off for a single small request, given the currently resident model, prefix availability and host memory pressure?
items.next_test: Use recorded load/warm costs for a simple dispatch estimate before building a router; validate prospective warm and cold measurements separately.

items.observed: Selective comparison panels preceded the explicit prefix-warm protocol. Final panels use it, and the blocker final recipe also changed temperature after a retained failure.
items.open_question: How much of any later latency change is due to caching, sampling, task assistance or other recipe differences? Existing combined results do not isolate each contribution.
items.next_test: Only run matched ablations for an actionable decision; do not relabel old mixed-cache panels as fully warmed or attribute assisted-task gains to the model.

items.observed: Canonical greens have coexisted with missing deliverables, resource-cleanup defects and forbidden behavior. Current acceptance also uses source/handoff review and targeted isolated probes; subsidiary citation qualifications remain recorded.
items.open_question: Which recurring review findings can become mechanical checks without granting evaluated models access to evaluator authority?
items.next_test: Derive a narrow independent check from a demonstrated failure, preserve separate isolation, and compare it with sealed prior review decisions. Strong-model judging remains a future option, not a demonstrated replacement.

items.observed: The final champion panels test repeated seeds on exposed task families. Retired Markdown and bundle-reader diagnostics failed for the tested recipes; task labels such as reserved no longer imply fresh exposure.
items.open_question: Do selected champions transfer to fresh tasks, and do future improvements also recover these preserved diagnostics?
items.next_test: Blind-review and seal new public tasks and independent solutions before evaluator feedback. Keep retired diagnostics separate and avoid treating task assistance as a model-only improvement.
